reasoning.text: The render passes both acceptance tests: the ISO shows the open butterfly array with no opaque block hiding a subsystem, TOP shows all eight blue BRAM banks, the orange DSP multiplier column, the symmetric add/sub clusters, the two distinct reduction members, the right-edge controllers, both white FIFOs, and the brass twiddle feeder L; FRONT/SIDE show the exploded butterfly lane and seven-fin exploded heatsink on their risers, all seated on the ground line. The only weaknesses left were the three carried-over nits — an incomplete dataflow triad (only twiddle and return drawn), materially identical add/sub members, and the exploded lane occluding central lanes in TOP — each individually worth under two points. Also corrected a prior scoring error where self_consistency was reported as 6 against a max of 5.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder and subtractor, then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, capped with a return arrow at the crossbar end to close the conflict-free read-modify-write loop. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset in Z so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
